answer.rationale: Routing a settlement peak's heavy writes through a release we cannot revert, while latency climbs on the write path, argues for absorbing throughput rather than shifting it. The release route is blocked by compliance (security patch must not be reverted), regional_failover risks in-flight settlement writes (per objective) and circuit_breaker / route_read_replicas would shed or only indirectly relieve a write-bound problem. Sized the add_capacity step to add headroom fast under peak load based on the memory_b3 pattern in which provisioning headroom kept queue depth flat across a promotional window; will verify memory_b3 for whether that result was achievable reactively as well as proactively, and memory_b5 as a secondary check (read offload) before deciding if read pressure is contributing to write p99. Stop the window after this single action if latency recovers toward target; otherwise revisit only after the next window opens.
